Hyperinsulinemia is an independent marker that predicts the development of atherosclerosis. A causal relationship between
hypertension and hyperinsulinemia has not yet been well established. Hypertension associated with hyperinsulinemia could be
due to increased renal sodium retention, increased intracellular free calcium, increased sympathetic nervous system activity, or
increased intraabdominal pressure because of increased visceral fat deposition.
